nodes.label: desktop memory - the v2 graph spine

Frozen copy taken 2026-08-03 of the desktop machine's memory file - the live directory sits on the other machine and is not reachable from here, so this copy is what there is to review. Listed unreviewed in REVIEW_REGISTER.md section 6. The v2 graph spine, user-decided 2026-06-12: Source to File to Chunk to Tag, and nothing else is a node - superseding the 2026-05-30 drafted model with entity nodes per record, :Employee/:Customer/:PrAuthor nodes and :COVERS edges. The node/attribute rule, the lens every candidate runs through: a thing is a node only when others depend on its facts to resolve themselves or retrieval walks THROUGH it, and an attribute when it is a value you filter or boost by - born from the user's 'either they are nodes, but then we get edges to EVERY fucking chunk, or they are just attributes'. What the rule decided: File is a node, because it is the resolution catalog every reference depends on and the hash must have one authoritative copy; Chunk is the finest node, with hard-field values riding as indexed chunk attributes; record nodes are CUT, because most of them would be a chunk giving two almost-same nodes, so records stay addressable via json_pointer references with no :COVERS edges; branch and collection positions are attributes rather than nodes, since the tree lives in the path attribute; entity and metadata nodes - Employee, Customer, org hierarchy - are CUT, with the hierarchy living in the raw metadata files read through references at query time, because the graph must not mirror the directories, which the file records as assistant inertia the user killed; the chunk-to-file relevance weight is DEAD, the containment edge carrying no number, since its v1 job of demoting filler is solved by coherence-episode chunking while typicality actively hurts by burying the rare relevant aside; and tag nodes are per-chunk emissions rather than shared vocabulary, user-decided 2026-06-13, each emitted tag its own node bound to exactly one chunk, which kills the v1 residue channel where shared tags minted from oracle chunks survived the herb-eval filter.
